speaker: D. A. Kazhdan
title: Ihara: curves, coverings, and congruence monodromy
summary: The actual heading is on P000253. Kazhdan identifies Ihara by journal and pages 107--121, then begins the analogy between hyperbolic uniformization and curves over finite fields. The surviving mathematical content is introductory: coordinate rings, points, morphisms, and unramified fibres. None of Ihara\textquoteright s three precise congruence-monodromy conjectures is written out, so they are not imported into the problem index. The paper was received in August 1967 and published in 1968 \citep[Introduction]{ihara1968monodromy}.

speaker: V. P. Palamodov
title: Jets along the diagonal and the Spencer complex
summary: The talk begins on P000254 and continues on P000255. Palamodov introduces jets and the trivial Spencer resolution; Gelfand reformulates jets as functions modulo powers of the diagonal ideal and sketches a many-point version. Sweeney, Malgrange, and Quillen are bibliographical leads. The explicit Sweeney citation resolves to \citet[Chapter~I]{sweeney1968neumann}; the notebook does not specify which Malgrange or Quillen work it means.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Traces of integral operators with operator-valued kernels
summary: On P000256 Kirillov states a trace formula for a weakly jointly continuous operator-valued kernel and singles out positivity for the converse. This is an exact match to Lemma~8 of \citet[pp.~49--50 of the Russian original]{kirillov1968characters}. That paper had already appeared in issue~2 of 1968, so this occurrence is expository (E), even though its 1967 announcement may have class~A. The catalogue date is retained; 27 October 1968 was Sunday, and the notebook date is not silently shifted to Monday.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Schedule notices; no separately identifiable intervention
summary: The catalogue supplies a separate Gelfand record, but P000256 names Kirillov and Weinstein and contains scheduling notes (Kirillov on traces, a skipped meeting, and Kazhdan on Dwork). No independent mathematical passage is explicitly attributed to Gelfand in the surviving page. This record is retained as a plan with uncertain attribution and receives no invented occurrence item.

speaker: Alan Weinstein [catalogue attribution; probably Alexander Weinstein]
title: Intermediate eigenvalue problems and a delay-equation notice
summary: The actual passage on P000256--P000257 concerns Rayleigh quotients, finite-dimensional constraints, and lower spectral bounds through intermediate problems. These are Alexander Weinstein\textquoteright s subject, with a directly matching 1963 paper, whereas the catalogue says Alan Weinstein; the scan says only Prof.~Weinstein (USA). The name is therefore not silently emended. A separate brief notice on P000257 attributes periodic delay equations and control applications to a Polish speaker, written Rolevich; its precise attribution and theorem are unresolved.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Characters, coadjoint orbits, and Plancherel measure
summary: The actual talk occupies P000257--P000260. It moves from distribution characters and the affine group to symplectic coadjoint orbits, orbital Fourier transforms, integrality, the compact rank-one example, and Plancherel measure. A Pfaffian exercise and brief remarks on matrix products, tensor products, and Rodrigues formulas close the page. The unrestricted all-group wording is separated from the nilpotent and compact theorems actually established in \citet{kirillov1962unitary,kirillov1968characters}.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: A graded reading programme in representation theory
summary: The programme runs from P000261 to the upper part of P000263. Level zero covers finite and compact groups, rotations, and Lie algebras; level one proceeds through classical unitary representations, characters, induction, nilpotent groups, rank-one examples, and operator algebras. Level two adds non-Archimedean groups, symmetric-space Plancherel theory, horospheres, Borel--Weil, type-I theory, enveloping algebras, orbit methods, Kazhdan\textquoteright s work, and lattices. The closing promise of a list in Uspekhi is a publication plan, not the list itself. Individual bibliography entries without mathematical assertions are preserved here rather than inflated into occurrence items.

speaker: M. L. Gromov
title: Differential relations, local flexibility, and global existence
summary: Gromov begins in the lower half of P000263 and continues through P000266. Jets turn PDEs into differential relations; deformation lifting replaces uniqueness, and local solvability plus suitable invariance is proposed as the route to global solutions. The precise open-manifold theorem appears in \citet[Theorem~4.1.1]{gromov1969stable}, received 8 July 1968 and published in 1969. The closing isometric-mapping statements have illegible dimensions and missing hypotheses and are not all identified with that theorem.

speaker: O. A. Oleinik
title: Radkevich on hypoelliptic second-order operators
summary: Oleinik\textquoteright s heading is on P000267, before Kazhdan\textquoteright s heading on P000268, despite the catalogue numbering. She reviews H\"ormander\textquoteright s sum-of-squares criterion and announces a symbol-derivative/commutator approach for general nonnegative second-order forms. Radkevich\textquoteright s short paper was received 19 November 1968, six days before the talk, and printed in 1969 \citep{radkevich1969hormander}. Gelfand\textquoteright s question about locally integrable solutions at the top of P000268 belongs here.

speaker: D. A. Kazhdan
title: Dwork rationality and non-Archimedean Fredholm theory
summary: The heading begins after Gelfand\textquoteright s intervention on P000268 and the talk continues through P000271. Closed-point Euler products and extension-field point counts lead to Dwork\textquoteright s rationality theorem and the Borel--Dwork criterion. The final page supplies the non-Archimedean tools: compact operators, Fredholm determinants, Teichm\"uller representatives, analytic zeros, and integrality of reciprocal roots. These are an exposition of work already published in 1960--1962, not new conjectures of November 1968.
The year heading marks the calendar transition to the meeting dated 10 February 1969 on P000272. It contains no independent mathematical assertion and receives no occurrence item.

speaker: G. A. Margulis
title: Counting orbit points in a hyperbolic disc
summary: The Margulis passage is only the opening part of P000272; Gelfand\textquoteright s 3-adic arithmetic begins on the same page and belongs to record167. The notice describes lifts of a point to the universal cover, a leading count expressed through area and boundary length, a claimed square-root remainder, and the use of horocycle ergodicity. The leading asymptotic has an exact 1969 publication match; the claimed error requires separate treatment. Linnik\textquoteright s sphere-point work is invoked as an analogy, not a theorem transferring one count to the other.
